==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|autum||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|autumpne}}, from {{der|en|frm|automne}}, from {{der|en|fro|automne}}, {{m|fro|autonne}}, from {{der|en|la|autumnus}}. Some of the  verbal senses are from {{der|en|la|autumnāre}}.<ref>{{R:OED2|pos=v|id=00015283}}</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ôʹtəm}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɔːtəm/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-autumn.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɔtəm/|[ˈɔɾɪ̈m]|[ˈɔɾm̩]|a=GA}}
*** {{audio|en|En-US constrastive autumn.ogg|a=US,non-cot-caught}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɑtəm/|[ˈɑɾɪ̈m]|[ˈɑɾm̩]|a=cot-caught}}
*** {{audio|en|en-us-autumn.ogg|a=US,cot-caught}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-autumn.wav|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔːtəm|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|au|tumn}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}
[[File:Autumn leaves, Talcott Mountain State Park.jpg|thumb|'''Autumn''' in the United States]]

# {{senseid|en|Q1314}}Traditionally the third of the four [[season]]s, when [[deciduous]] trees lose their leaves, and temperatures and daylight hours decrease; typically regarded as spanning the months of [[September]], [[October]], and [[November]] in the [[Northern Hemisphere]], and the months of [[March]], [[April]] and [[May]] in the [[Southern Hemisphere]].
#: {{syn|en|fall<q:North America>|harvest<q:UK dialect>|back end<q:UK dialect>}}
#: {{co|en|'''autumn''' leaves}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|act=II|scene=i|page=149|column=1|passage=The Spring, the Sommer, / The childing '''Autumne''', angry Winter change / Their wonted Liueries, {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=In the '''autumn''' there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been started for them and all but a few joined. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.}}
#* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text=Serene, smiling, enigmatic, she faced him with no fear whatever showing in her dark eyes. The clear light of the bright '''autumn''' morning had no terrors for youth and health like hers.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=2000|title={{w|Stan (song)|Stan}}|artist=w:Eminem|album=w:The Marshall Mathers LP|passage=I left my cell, my pager, and my home phone at the bottom / I sent two letters back in '''autumn''', you must not've got 'em}}
# {{label|en|by extension}} The time period when someone or something is past its prime.
#: {{syn|en|decline}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|passage=She has beauty still, and if it be not in its heyday, it is not yet in its '''autumn'''. }}
# {{lb|en|fashion}} A person with relatively dark hair and a warm skin tone, seen as best suited to certain colours in clothing.

====Usage notes====
* {{season name spelling}}
* Outside of North America, ''autumn'' is generally the only name for the season. In the United States and Canada, both ''autumn'' and {{m|en|fall|id=autumn}} are used, the former being perhaps felt as the more formal term and the latter as the more colloquial or everyday term.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[spend]] the autumn (in a particular place).
#* {{quote-book|en|author=William C[yrus] Sprague|title=Tad, the Story of a Boy who Had No Chance|year=1912|page=2|passage=If Tad’s father and Tad had wintered, springed, summered, and '''autumned''' together for an hundred years instead of fifteen they could{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To (cause to) undergo the changes associated with autumn, such as leaves changing color and falling from trees.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Horace Eaton Walker|title=The Lady of Dardale and Other Poems|location=Manchester, N.H.|publisher=Browne & Rowe|year=1886|pages=139 and 201|passage=The glistening path where weeds had clung, / And tumbled bushes lay, / Was hidden now, but yet there rung / Tones of an '''autumned''' May.{{...}}And cheers rang out, the song and shout, / For the fray had found its eve, / And pirate chief like '''autumned''' leaf, / O’er fallen pride did grieve!”}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=w:Virginia Sandars|title=The Duke of Melton|journal=w:London Society|volume=LII|location=London|publisher=F. V. White & Co.|year=1887|page=185|passage={{...}}he himself roamed with innocent Kate through the fast '''autumning''' woods{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Jeffrey Winterborne|title=Medical Marijuana / Cannabis Cultivation: Trees of Life at the University of London|publisher=Pukka Press|year=2008|pages=249–250|isbn=978-0-9550112-2-1|passage={{...}}three quarters, two thirds of the flowering tops have changed colour and these are very resinous, solid buds and the colouration of the leaf, you can see how it’s yellowed off, it’s '''autumning''', autumn has come if you would like to put it that way.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Joyce Rupp|title=Anchors for the Soul: Daily Wisdom for Inspiration and Guidance|location=Notre Dame, Ind.|publisher=Sorin Books|year=2018|pages=8 and 9|isbn=978-1-932057-13-3|passage=Spirit of Autumn, When I grow tired of using my gifts to benefit others, take me to the '''autumned''' fields where earth freely yields the bounty of her summer.{{...}}All night a steady rain fell upon the '''autumned''' earth, moistening every dried crack of the bony summer, rinsing what lay tattered and soiled in the remnants of yesterday.}}
